lines: The app ships no composer/autoload.php, so the server registers its generic loader for lib/ and looks every class up in the file system.

A composer/composer.json with config.vendor-dir ".", config.optimize-autoloader true, a config.autoloader-suffix and autoload.psr-4 {"OCA\\CAFeVDBMembers\\": "../lib/"} makes composer dump-autoload write composer/autoload.php with a class map; the code of the app does not change.
11 uses of the private API of the server in 6 files. Only OCP and NCU are public: what is below OC changes without notice between majors.

1 class implements or extends what the public API marks #[Consumable] in a major of Nextcloud 35: an app calls it, and the server may add a method to it in any release, which breaks a class that implements it.

3 transactions are opened and closed by hand. The trait TTransactional has atomic() since Nextcloud 24 and atomicRetry() since Nextcloud 27, which repeats a transaction that ran into a deadlock, as the manual recommends.
lib/ reads the clock directly in 5 places. OCP\AppFramework\Utility\ITimeFactory, a PSR-20 ClockInterface, gives the same time and can be replaced in a test.

The app reads and writes its app config in 23 places and registers no config lexicon, which IRegistrationContext::registerConfigLexicon() takes since Nextcloud 31. A lexicon states the type, the default and the sensitivity of each key in one place.

1 place states routes that are no constants, so this cannot read them: the server builds them at run time. The inventory lacks them, and what depends on the full list of routes is left out: route-unreferenced, ocs-unreferenced, frontend-url-without-route, controller-method-unrouted and the operations of openapi-drift that no route provides.
